scope: iPhone 17 Pro Simulator (stock runtime, Release BananaModelTests), MailColdStartCostTests. One mailbox on disk: 180,000 conversations in two accounts, 540,000 message rows, write-ahead log checkpointed as the app writer keeps it. Each process opens the existing mailbox; within a process the five iterations reopen the stores, so iteration 1 is the fresh-process cost and 2-5 reuse warm process state. The OS file cache is warm in every process. Steps follow MailApplication.start(): open the four stores and the intent store, make MailLiveSource, prepareActions, make it visible, first 50 unified-Inbox rows. Simulator timings run on Mac cores and are lower than a phone.
result: Two startup reads walked every message: the action coordinator looked for messages with a local overlay by scanning message, and the held-removal count let SQLite drive its join from message. Walking the overlay and forcing the join to start from held_removal took prepareActions from 98-100 to 43-47 ms in a fresh process and from 74-79 to 12-13 ms on later opens. Launch to the first inbox rows went from 132-136 to 84-99 ms in a fresh process.
artifactsExcluded: A first fixture without message rows hid both scans. A second fixture left its 361 MB bulk insert in the write-ahead log, which every fresh process replayed while opening index.sqlite (about 100 ms); the app writer checkpoints above 8 MiB, so the measured fixture is checkpointed.
